item.title: Nepal floods: Rescuers struggle to locate power plants to find trapped survivors
item.description: Nearly a week after flash floods devastated parts of Nepal and Tibet, rescuers are still searching for people trapped in hydropower plants. But first they have to find the plants.
item.content:encoded: Nearly a week after flash floods devastated parts of Nepal and Tibet, rescuers are still searching for people trapped in hydropower plants. But first they have to find the plants.

item.title: How Dolly Parton's literacy work affected Indigenous communities in Australia
item.description: In Australia, the queen of country music, Dolly Parton, is being remembered for her work in advancing children's literacy, particularly in Indigenous communities.

item.title: Judge hears final arguments before deciding charges for accused killer of Charlie Kirk
item.description: A judge in Utah is expected to formally charge the man accused of shooting conservative activist Charlie Kirk with murder, and whether his sentence could include the death penalty.

item.title: More school districts are shrinking. New research asks whether closures work
item.description: School districts across the country are closing campuses as enrollment falls. New research says the financial savings may be smaller than expected.

item.title: 'Damage happened here.' In Marlon James' new novel, the violence has a point
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with award-winning author Marlon James about his new book, The Disappearers, the story of a brutal attack on a group of gay men in Jamaica and its aftermath.

item.title: The Clancy jury continues to deliberate
item.description: The jury in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the mother charged with murdering her three children, said it's not yet come to an unanimous decision. The judge has urged them to keep trying.

item.title: There's a new partner for the U.S. Venezuela oil deal. Energy experts are skeptical
item.description: The White House has confirmed the Venezuelan company that says it will work with the U.S. to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves. Energy experts are skeptical that it's up for the task.

item.title: In Massachusetts' primary, Sen. Ed Markey seeks to fend off Rep. Seth Moulton
item.description: In Massachusetts' Democratic Primary, generational change is being debated, spurred by Rep. Seth Moulton's challenge to the incumbent, Sen. Ed Markey, as well as who can carry on a progressive agenda.

item.title: Flash floods shaping America's national story
item.description: Amid floods in Nepal, the U.S. is experiencing serious floods in the west, including the Grand Canyon. We break down if they are connected and how Americans can understand this monsoon season.

item.title: Milwaukee's Veggie Chop Shop uses farmers' excess produce to feed those in need
item.description: A program called the Veggie Chop Shop enlists volunteers to gather extra produce from farmers' markets that would otherwise go to waste. They then cook meals for people facing food insecurity.
